text: In California, if your work hours leave you no time to vote in a statewide election, you can take up to 2 hours off to vote without losing pay.
seenIn: a coworker at your campus job

room.label: students (demo crowd)
room.note: No published poll has measured this belief yet. The 5C pilot survey replaces this split with real student answers.

truthSource.label: California Secretary of State: Time Off to Vote notice
truthSource.oneLine: If you don’t have enough time outside working hours to vote in a statewide election, California law lets you take up to two hours off to vote without losing pay. Tell your employer two working days ahead.

lesson.tip: Real worker protections can sound made up. This one has conditions: no time to vote outside work, notice two working days ahead, and time off at the start or end of a shift. Look for the notice employers must post.
